summary: Benoist proves that a Brauer class on a real surface has index equal to its period when it vanishes at every real point (Theorems 0.3 and 0.4), computes the index of unramified classes (Theorem 0.5), and deduces u(K) ≤ 4 for fields of transcendence degree 2 over R (Theorem 0.12, the case i = 2 of Pfister's conjecture) and the corresponding case of Lang's conjecture (Theorem 0.10). The proof pulls back along ramified double covers that satisfy a real Noether–Lefschetz criterion. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and nineteen findings are recorded. Propositions 4.4, 4.5 and 6.6 are not established as stated (E3, E4), and §3.1's cover is not finite (E1); the main theorems use only the repaired uniform case. Not formalised.

conventions.base: R means the actual real numbers except where explicitly replaced by an arbitrary real closed field. A smooth connected projective R-surface need not be geometrically connected. H^i(Y) without coefficients means F2-cohomology.
conventions.G: G=Gal(C/R)=C2 with generator conjugation σ; H_G denotes Borel/Grothendieck equivariant sheaf cohomology, not merely invariants of ordinary cohomology.
conventions.twists: Benoist uses Z(j)=i^j Z with σ=(-1)^j; parity determines its G-module. Identify with the 2πi normalization in Benoist2018 by an explicit rescaling, not literal equality of embedded lattices.
conventions.Brauer: For smooth integral X use Br(X)=H²_et(X,G_m), torsion here by injection into Br(k(X)). Field algebraic/cohomological comparison is a separate imported theorem. Multiplicative Lean Brauer identity 1 corresponds to additive paper 0.

items.name: Ramified double-cover family and its resolution
items.statement: Let S be a smooth connected projective real surface, R an SNC divisor, L a line bundle, r its divisor equation, and B the sections s of L²(R) whose divisor D is smooth and transverse to R away from Sing R. In X̄=P_S(O⊕L), with tautological v,w, set T̄={rv²=sw²}; resolve its ordinary double points above Sing R to T and let p:T→S. Blowing up the fixed singular points of X̄ embeds the family T in B×X. On a clopen real subset Psi with no real point upstairs, conjugation exchanges the two sheets, so Q has stabilizer action -1 and Q(1) has stabilizer action +1. The ordinary local system on Psi may still have nontrivial sign monodromy. The map phi:Q(1)→F2 is its canonical modulo2 map.
items.locator: §2.2, §7.1 and (2.11)–(2.12); specialized to the cover in §4
items.proof: The difference of the two sheet coefficients identifies the quotient with Z; exchange negates it, while sum and difference agree modulo2. Tensoring the conjugation sign changes its stabilizer action, not the ordinary monodromy.

items.name: First component under constant real evaluation
items.statement: In items158–160 with n=2 and V=U0, suppose a_1|Psi=0 and a_0|Psi=t for one constant t∈F2. Then eta_1|Psi=t[e]_1|Psi, where e is the double-cover class. If lambda∈Pic(S) extends the line bundle supplied by Lemma2.1 on S*, this is t cl_R(lambda)|Psi. The assertion also holds on Psi∩U0(R) and then extends over finitely many missing points when both sides extend.
items.locator: Derived from (2.12), Lemma2.1 and the trace quotient; BW1 (1.33)
items.proof: An integral Z(1)-class in degree2 has component0 equal to0. Hence phi(zeta)_0=t. For the rank-one ordinary system F underlying Q(1)|Psi, formula(2.12) with k=2,j=0 says phi(zeta)_1=beta_F(t). Since t is constant, its ordinary Bockstein is0; twisted Bockstein gives beta_F(t)=t[e]_1. Now a_1=eta_1-phi(zeta)_1=0. This is precisely where constant t is used; a variable component indicator cannot be replaced by a scalar multiplying a global Picard class.

items.name: Topological obstruction vanishes for uniform evaluation
items.statement: Under Assumptions3.1 and4.1, let a be the period-two Brauer class, aTilde its Kummer lift with component1 zero on Psi, and assume its component0 on Psi is one constant t∈F2. Conditional on the exact homological comparison item149 and the other cited inputs, the topological obstruction tau of p*a vanishes. This is the restricted form of Proposition4.4 needed by the main induction.
items.proof: In (4.8) the degree-one Bockstein calculation is [zeta]_1=t[e]_1, not [e]_1 in general. In the replacement preceding(4.6), use delta-((eta+t cl(lambda)) cup omega). The two resulting t[e]_1 contributions cancel modulo2. Then Assumption4.1(ii) supplies the curve correction, Proposition3.3 supplies the integral pushforward, and the exact diagram(4.2) gives tau=0. The typed comparison(4.5) itself remains conditional on G10.

items.name: Primitive Picard correction of the trace comparison
items.statement: Let n=2, let beta∈H²_G(T(C),Z(1)) lift p*a in the Brauer sequence, and let b be item159 on T_U0. Write beta|=b+2 gamma0+cl(phi0), and p_*beta=2 delta+cl(theta1). Then there is mu∈Pic(S) such that delta|-eta-p_*gamma0=cl(mu|U0). This uses the torsion-free COKERNEL of Pic(U0)→H²_G(U0(C),Z(1)).
items.locator: Typed replacement for Proposition4.5, pp.84–85; BW1 Proposition2.9
items.proof: The two classes beta| and b have the same Brauer image, so (2.17) supplies gamma0,phi0. Trace p*a=2a=0 supplies delta,theta1. Subtracting after trace yields 2(delta|-eta-p_*gamma0)=cl(p_*phi0-theta1|). Primitivity supplies mu0 on U0; extension of line bundles supplies mu on S. All operations are now integral.

api.name: picardTraceCorrection
api.statement: Return delta,theta1,gamma0,phi0,mu satisfying the two integral identities and the primitive divided identity.

items.name: Curve adjustment before applying the pushforward criterion
items.statement: Under Assumption4.1(ii), if d∈H²_G(S(C),Z(1)) has [d]_1|Psi=0, there is nu∈Pic(S), an integral linear combination of the allowed curves whose real loci avoid Psi, such that [d-cl(nu)]_1 is in p_*H¹(T(R),F2). If Proposition3.3 applies, d-cl(nu)=p_*gamma for an integral gamma upstairs.
items.locator: Assumption4.1(ii), Proposition3.3 and the last step of Proposition4.5
items.proof: Kernel generation is a sum of the pushforward subspace and curve classes. Lift its finite F2-linear combination of curves to a Picard class and subtract that class. Then apply the exact integral pushforward image statement; kernel membership alone does not give a pushforward.

items.name: Integral pushforward adjustment for uniform evaluation
items.statement: Under item162 hypotheses, for any integral beta lifting p*a, there exist gamma∈H²_G(T(C),Z(1)) and theta∈Pic(S) such that p_*(beta-2gamma)=cl(theta). This restricted Proposition4.5 uses no integral lift of aTilde downstairs. Its existence of beta is conditional on item162; its trace adjustment follows from the explicit inputs below.
items.locator: New conditional repair of Proposition4.5, pp.84–85
items.proof: Take the data from item163 and lambda from item161. The real first component of delta-cl(mu+t lambda) is zero on Psi∩U0, hence on Psi by finite-point removal. Apply item164 to obtain nu,gamma with p_*gamma=delta-cl(mu+t lambda+nu). Set theta=theta1+2mu+2t lambda+2nu. Substitution gives the conclusion. The extra nu is required by Assumption4.1(ii).

items.name: Degree-two splitting under uniform evaluation
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of item85, additionally require [aTilde]_0|Psi to be constant t∈F2. Conditional on the geometric/Hodge inputs and item149, there is a generically degree-two morphism p:T→S with T smooth connected projective, a_R(T)=0, and p(T(R)) disjoint from Psi. In this statement Psi may contain zero-evaluation components; t=0 is allowed.
items.locator: Proposition6.6 with the additional uniformity hypothesis and repaired inputs
items.proof: The branch construction establishes Assumptions3.1 and4.1. Use items162,165 in place of the unrestricted Propositions4.4–4.5. The real Green cone and integral lattice correction then make beta-2gamma-2delta a real integral(1,1) class; divisor algebraicity and (2.17) split a. The deformation continues to avoid Psi. These latter geometric inputs are the original proof, not newly certified prerequisites.

items.name: Uniform evaluation of the half-period class
items.statement: Let alpha have even period n and let Psi be its nonzero evaluation locus, contained in the unramified open. The period-two class a=(n/2)alpha has evaluation a_0=(n/2 mod2) on every point of Psi, and zero outside Psi. Consequently item166 applies with t=1 when n≡2 mod4, and with t=0 when n≡0 mod4. For the latter case Theta(a) is empty although Psi=Theta(alpha) need not be empty.
items.locator: Corrected dependency analysis of Proposition6.7, p.95
items.proof: Evaluation is a group homomorphism to Br(R)=Z/2. On Psi, alpha evaluates to its unique nonzero element. Multiply it by n/2. Kummer component0 is this evaluation. No integral-lift premise on S is inferred.

items.name: Existing quadratic algebra and its rank-two basis
items.statement: For a commutative ring A and a∈A, QuadraticAlgebra A a 0 has elements x+yω, multiplication ω²=a, and the A-basis (1,ω). It is finite free of rank two even when a=0; freeness does not imply reducedness or étaleness.

items.name: Existing quadratic trace, norm and discriminant
items.statement: For x+yω in QuadraticAlgebra A a 0, the library trace is2x, norm is x²−ay², and polynomial discriminant is4a. The norm equals the determinant of multiplication. The trace-zero splitting used below requires2 invertible.

items.name: Hypersurfaces supply the S2 input
items.statement: A quotient of a regular Noetherian local ring by one nonzerodivisor is Cohen–Macaulay. In particular the local rings of a hypersurface in a smooth variety satisfy S2.
items.locator: Shared R03.3 complete-intersection supplier; also PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/087
proofSteps: Import the regular-sequence and complete-intersection Cohen–Macaulay theorem from R03.3. This is an explicit unbuilt supplier, not a fresh private depth theory.

items.name: Serre normality criterion
items.statement: A Noetherian ring is normal exactly when its localizations at primes of height at most one are regular and it satisfies S2.
items.locator: Stacks031S, full statement and displayed proof read; shared Bockle–Iyengar–Paskunas23/087 supplier
proofSteps: Use the shared R03.3 normality contract already requested by BIP23. Stacks031S proves the equivalence by induction and a finite integral extension argument. Its transitive depth/local-ring inputs remain with that owner; they are not credited as built.

items.name: Blowup charts and strict transforms
items.statement: The blowup of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal is relative Proj of its Rees algebra, with projective universal property, affine charts, flat base change and isomorphism where the ideal is invertible. Charts are the Rees charts, with torsion removed as required; adjoining ratios without the necessary cancellation need not give them.
items.locator: Upstream StableReduction Layer4; accepted AUDIT02 says the scheme blowup package is not built
proofSteps: Consume the upstream construction. R09.7a uses the same supplier; no second blowup or surface-resolution carrier is introduced.

items.name: Proper birational maps to a normal scheme preserve functions
items.statement: Let h:Y→Z be proper and birational between integral Noetherian schemes, with Y reduced and Z normal. Then h_*O_Y=O_Z and h has geometrically connected fibres. Apply this componentwise for a finite disjoint union of normal components.
items.locator: Stacks0AY8 and03H0/03H2; shared Witaszek22 Stein-factorization supplier
proofSteps: Use the shared Stein factorization. Its finite intermediate scheme has the same rational function field as the normal target, hence is the target. Stacks0AY8 states the stronger generic-fibre criterion with the reducedness and generic-point conditions explicit.

In the application, normality and the explicit local models verify these hypotheses. The local Cech calculation185 also verifies the structure-sheaf identity directly. The general theorem is an outstanding supplier request, not a theorem newly owned by the surface application.

items.name: Finite cover associated with the branch product
items.statement: Let S be a smooth surface over a characteristic-zero field, R an SNC divisor with section r of O(R), L invertible, and s∈H0(S,L²(R)) with smooth divisor D meeting R transversely and avoiding Sing R. Put M=L(R) and b=rs∈H0(S,M²). Define C=Spec_S(O_S⊕M⁻¹), where multiplication M⁻²→O_S is contraction with b. It is finite locally free of rank2, locally z²=rs. It is étale precisely away from R∪D.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: Use the existing quadratic algebra on each trivialization: (a,u)(a′,u′)=(aa′+buu′,au′+a′u). Under a frame change of M, both the root and coefficient transform with the prescribed first and second powers, so these algebras glue.

The basis gives local rank2 and therefore finiteness and flatness through the SF0 affine-morphism dictionary. The relative differentials are generated by dz with2z dz=0; because2 is invertible the étale locus is the complement of b=0.
This is the explicit b=rs specialization of the trace-zero double-cover formalism also used by EVW16/136. Generic relative Spec, line bundles and descent remain shared SF0/SF3 suppliers.

items.name: Normality of the SNC branch cover
items.statement: The finite cover C of174 is normal. Its only singularities are ordinary double points over Sing(R∪D). If the branch is empty, C can be disconnected; normality does not assert that its total space is integral.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: Locally C is a hypersurface in the total space of M, hence S2 by170.

Off the branch, the morphism is étale over smooth S. At a smooth branch point use b as a local parameter up to a unit; the equation has a nonzero transverse derivative and is regular. Thus all codimension-one points are regular. Apply171.

At a branch crossing choose local parameters u,v and absorb the unit coefficient into one parameter; this gives an étale-local equation z²=uv. Its unique singular point is the origin and its tangent cone is the nondegenerate ternary quadratic z²−uv.

items.name: Map from the projective model to the finite cover
items.statement: In the notation174 let Tbar⊂P_S(O⊕L) be rv²=sw² with the paper’s tautological sections. There is a morphism h:Tbar→C defined on w≠0 by z=r(v/w) and on v≠0 by z=s(w/v). It is proper and an isomorphism away from R∩D. In particular it is an isomorphism near Sing R, where s is a unit.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: The two expressions are sections of the pullback of M and agree where both coordinates are nonzero, since rv²=sw². Both square to rs. This gives the morphism to the relative spectrum.
On r invertible the inverse has [v:w]=[z:r]. On s invertible it has [v:w]=[s:z], expressed in the corresponding trivializations. These inverses agree on overlap.
The projective hypersurface is proper over S and C is separated over S; the graph factorization makes h proper. The unit-locus inverse gives birationality on each component.

items.name: The partial resolution at R intersect D
items.statement: At a crossing of R and D, Tbar is smooth and h resolves the node z²=rs. Its two charts are (r,x), with s=rx²,z=rx, and (s,y), with r=sy²,z=sy. They glue by y=x⁻¹ and s=rx². The exceptional fibre is P1 with normal bundle O_P1(−2). Equivalently this is the blowup of the local ideal(r,z) in the node.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: Since r,s form an étale local coordinate pair, the first chart equation rx²=s eliminates s and the second eliminates r. Both charts are smooth.

In the Rees charts for(r,z), cancellation in the integral node algebra gives z=rx,s=rx² and r=sy²,z=sy. Include this cancellation; the unsaturated relation r(rx²−s)=0 would introduce a false component.
At r=s=0 the coordinates x,y give two affine lines glued by y=x⁻¹. The conormal generators r and s satisfy s=x²r, giving O(2) conormal and O(−2) normal. The argument descends from the local charts.

items.name: Fixed singular centres of the projective family
items.statement: The singular points of Tbar are exactly the points over Sing R with w=0, equivalently [v:w]=[1:0]. Their locations in P_S(O⊕L) are independent of s∈B. The phrase v vanishes on published p77 must read w vanishes.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: Above Sing R, s is nonzero because D avoids Sing R. Hence rv²=sw² forces w=0, while v is nonzero. In the chart v=1 the equation is r=s y².
Write r=unit*u*v locally at an SNC crossing and divide by the unit s. The singularity is the ordinary double point uv=y² at u=v=y=0. The point in the ambient bundle depends only on R.
At a smooth branch point the local derivative is nonzero. At R∩D use177. Away from the branch the cover is étale. These cases exhaust S and exclude additional singular points.

items.name: Blowing up the split ordinary double point
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field k, blow up the vertex of Spec k[u,v,z]/(uv−z²). The result is smooth, with two affine charts v=u a²,z=u a and u=v b²,z=v b; the exceptional conic UV=Z² is split and isomorphic to P1_k. The chart with distinguished z lies in their union. These calculations commute with the étale base changes used here.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: In the u-chart substitute v=u V,z=u a and take the strict transform V=a². The v-chart is symmetric. In the z-chart the strict transform is UV=1, so both U,V are units and this chart is already covered.

The exceptional divisor is the smooth conic UV=Z² in P2. The map [a:b]↦[a²:b²:ab] identifies it with P1, over k itself. Its smoothness and the affine charts prove resolution. This is the n=2 local calculation already in the upstream blowup direction.

items.name: Finite Stein model and function splitting
items.statement: Let T be obtained from Tbar by blowing up its ordinary double points above Sing R. Then p:T→S factors as T→C→S, with C the normal finite flat rank-two model174. Both T→C and Tbar→C preserve the structure sheaf and have geometrically connected fibres. Thus C=Spec_S(p_*O_T), and p_*O_T=O_S⊕L⁻¹(−R), compatibly with the involution.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: The first map is proper and is an isomorphism away from the finite crossing set. At R∩D it is the resolution177; at Sing R use the isomorphism176 followed by179. Every exceptional geometric fibre is P1.
Apply173 to each normal component; alternatively185 computes the function algebra locally and commutes with the required flat base changes. The same argument applies to the partial resolution Tbar→C.
Push the structure sheaf along the finite map C→S and use174. This proves the relative-Spec identity defining the finite Stein model; no global finiteness of p:T→S is asserted.

items.name: Correct finite-flat and exceptional strata
items.statement: For the resolved cover p:T→S, put Delta=R∪D, S0=S minus Sing Delta, and S*=S minus Delta. The restriction over S0 is finite locally free of rank2; that over S* is finite étale of degree2. At each geometric point of Sing Delta its fibre is P1. Over a smooth branch point the scheme fibre is length2 and nonreduced, so geometric point counts do not express flat degree.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: Away from the crossings the resolutions are isomorphisms, so transfer174. The relative differential calculation gives the étale restriction.
At R∩D use177 and at Sing R use179. Since D is smooth and avoids Sing R, these are all the crossing points. This is precisely the exceptional set used in the support sequences of §3.3.

items.name: Resolved family in the corrected fixed ambient blowup
items.statement: For the open set B of sections in174, blow up P_S(O⊕L) at the fixed points over Sing R with w=0. The strict transforms of the hypersurfaces rv²=sw² form a smooth projective family over B in this fixed blown-up threefold. Over R∩D the original hypersurfaces are already smooth and no additional ambient centres are needed.
items.locator: Benoist §3.1–3.3 pp76–79; explicit local proof supplied in this continuation
proofSteps: Near each fixed centre, s is invertible on the entire chosen family neighbourhood. The local equation is a family of uv=unit*y² nodes. The blowup calculation179, with the unit retained, gives charts smooth relative to B.

Away from these centres, all fibres of the hypersurface family are smooth by178; the relative Jacobian criterion verifies smoothness over B. The closed strict transform in the fixed projective ambient blowup gives projectivity.
The centres are the corrected w=0 points, not v=0. The parameter-dependent R∩D curves are part of each smooth fibre and are contracted only by its map to the finite model.

items.name: Strict-transform lifts of the auxiliary curve
items.statement: Let C0⊂S be smooth, meeting R transversely away from Sing R, and g∈H0(C0,L) have reduced zero divisor disjoint from R. If s|C0=a1*r*g² with a1>0 real, the two sections [v:w]=[±sqrt(a1)g:1] define closed curves in Tbar isomorphic to C0 and avoiding its singular locus. They lift unchanged to T. They meet where g=0 and are distinct over R∩C0. The full inverse image of C0 also contains the exceptional P1 fibres over R∩C0.
items.locator: Benoist §5.1 p86; corrected interpretation of the strict transform
proofSteps: Substitute either section into rv²=sw². A section of the projective bundle over the closed curve is a closed immersion, so each image is isomorphic to C0.

The coordinate w never vanishes; since all singular centres have w=0 the curves avoid them. On the complement of R the equation factors into the two indicated graph equations. Their closures are the strict-transform branches; no assertion that the full pullback is a finite union of only these graphs is made.
At a zero of g, the two graph points coincide at v=0; at R∩C0 the value of g is a unit, so they occupy two distinct points on the exceptional fibre.

items.name: Restriction of the trace-zero function summand
items.statement: For the plus lifted curve183, the restriction p_*O_T=O_S⊕M⁻¹→O_C0 is locally (a,b)↦a+sqrt(a1)*r*g*b. Consequently p_*O_T(−C0) is its kernel. The same assertion holds on Tbar. This uses left exactness of pushforward, not finiteness of p. Rescaling g by sqrt(a1) recovers the printed coefficient rg in(5.5).
proofSteps: On the w-chart the trace-zero root is z=r(v/w). Along the chosen graph it is sqrt(a1)rg; evaluate a+bz. This description respects the line-bundle twists.
Apply the left-exact functor p_* to0→O_T(−C0)→O_T→O_C0→0. Because the graph maps isomorphically to C0, the third sheaf is the indicated O_C0. No right-exactness claim is used.
The nonzero real scalar sqrt(a1) may be absorbed in g and does not change the injectivity test later in Lemma5.3; without that renormalization it belongs in the displayed arrow.

items.name: Local Cech calculation for the node resolution
items.statement: For the resolution of C=Spec k[r,s,z]/(rs−z²), use U=Spec k[r,x], V=Spec k[s,y] with s=rx²,z=rx,y=x⁻¹. Then Gamma(U union V,O)=k[r,rx,rx²]≅k[r,z,s]/(z²−rs), and H^i(U union V,O)=0 for i>0. Hence the resolution has h_*O=O_C and R^i h_*O=0 for i>0. These identities persist under flat base change.
items.locator: Explicit Cech proof for the node charts; applies to Benoist p87 rational-singularity use
proofSteps: The intersection is affine with ring k[r,x,x⁻¹]. The image of k[s,y] is spanned by monomials r^i x^j with i≥0 and j≤2i; the image of k[r,x] has j≥0.
Every Laurent monomial belongs to at least one image: use U if j≥0, V if j<0. Thus the degree-one Cech cokernel is zero; higher groups vanish for this two-affine cover with affine overlap.

The intersection of the two subrings has0≤j≤2i. If j=2b+c with c=0 or1, r^i x^j=r^(i−b−c)(rx)^c(rx²)^b. The exponent is nonnegative. These normal forms also prove the sole relation z²=rs and linear independence.

Quasi-coherent cohomology on this separated affine cover and its localization identify the sheaf direct images. Tensoring the exact Cech complex by a flat algebra preserves the calculation. This supplies the local vanishing for the étale node charts; it is not an assertion that all surface singularities are rational.

declarations.statementRead:
a structure with two fields, `re` and `im`. When `R` is a commutative ring, this is isomorphic to
`R[X]/(X^2-b*X-a)`. -/
@[ext]
structure QuadraticAlgebra (R : Type u) (a b : R) : Type u where
  /-- Real part of an element in quadratic algebra -/
  re : R
  /-- Imaginary part of an element in quadratic algebra -/
  im : R

@[simps]
def reₗ : QuadraticAlgebra R a b →ₗ[R] R where
  toFun := re
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _ := rfl

/-- `QuadraticAlgebra.im` as a `LinearMap` -/
@[simps]
def imₗ : QuadraticAlgebra R a b →ₗ[R] R where
  toFun := im
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _ := rfl

/-- `QuadraticAlgebra.equivTuple` as a `LinearEquiv` -/
def linearEquivTuple : QuadraticAlgebra R a b ≃ₗ[R] (Fin 2 → R) where
  __ := equivProd a b |>.trans <| finTwoArrowEquiv _ |>.symm
  map_add' _ _ := funext <| Fin.forall_fin_two.2 ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
  map_smul' _ _ := funext <| Fin.forall_fin_two.2 ⟨rfl, rfl⟩

@[simp]
lemma linearEquivTuple_apply (z : QuadraticAlgebra R a b) :
    (linearEquivTuple a b) z = ![z.re, z.im] := rfl

@[simp]
lemma linearEquivTuple_symm_apply (x : Fin 2 → R) :
    (linearEquivTuple a b).symm x = ⟨x 0, x 1⟩ := rfl

/-- The norm of an element in a quadratic algebra is the determinant of the endomorphism defined by
left multiplication by that element. -/
@[simp]
theorem det_toLinearMap_eq_norm (z : QuadraticAlgebra R a b) :
    (DistribSMul.toLinearMap R (QuadraticAlgebra R a b) z).det = z.norm := by
  rw [← LinearMap.det_toMatrix <| basis ..]
  have : !![z.re, a * z.im; z.im, z.re + b * z.im].det = z.norm := by
    simp [norm]
    ring
  convert! this
  apply LinearEquiv.eq_symm_apply _ |>.mp
  ext1 w
  apply basis .. |>.repr.injective
  apply DFunLike.coe_injective
  rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_symm, Matrix.repr_toLin]
  ext i

/-- The discriminant of the quadratic algebra `QuadraticAlgebra R a b`, that is, the
discriminant `b ^ 2 + 4 * a` of the polynomial `X ^ 2 - b * X - a`. -/
def discr [CommSemiring R] (a b : R) : R := b ^ 2 + 4 * a

theorem discr_def [CommSemiring R] (a b : R) : discr a b = b ^ 2 + 4 * a := rfl

/-- Under the change of generator `ω ↦ u • ω + k` (see `QuadraticAlgebra.changeGenerator`), the
discriminant is multiplied by `u ^ 2`. -/
theorem discr_changeGenerator [CommRing R] (a b u k : R) :
    discr (u ^ 2 * a - u * b * k - k ^ 2) (u * b + 2 * k) = u ^ 2 * discr a b := by
  rw [discr_def, discr_def]; ring
